---
title: "Research"
---

My research asks how much air pollution costs society in health and money, and what we gain when we reduce it.

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .theme-card}
### Air pollution epidemiology
Health effects of air pollutants such as NO₂ and PM~2.5~ across the life course, from pregnancy and childhood outcomes to ageing-related outcomes.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .theme-card}
### Health impact assessment
Estimating attributable burden and the health gains of interventions, drawing on HRAPIE-2 recommendations.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .theme-card}
### Lifetable & economic modelling
Life-years gained, QALYs and monetised benefits to support cost–benefit appraisal of environmental, climate change or Net-Zero policies.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .theme-card}
### Evidence synthesis
Systematic reviews and meta-analyses following PRISMA, including work on LLM-assisted literature screening and data extraction.
:::

:::

## Current projects

- **WellHome WP5**: Assessing the health and economic benefits of indoor air quality interventions such as a gas-to-electric cooker transition
- **Air pollution and childhood asthma development**: Systematic review on air pollution exposure and childhood asthma development, collaboration with UKHSA

## Grants and fundings

- **Dame Julia Higgins Postdoc Collaborative Research Fund, Imperial College London (2025-2026)**: PI, Automating Environmental Health Literature Screening Using Large Language Models. Co-investigators: Dr Ling Huang, Dr Sujin Kang
- **Pump Priming Award, MRC Centre for Environment and Health (2025-2026)**: PI, Analysing and improving the characterisation of the risk of lung cancer associated with air pollution exposure among never-smokers 
- **PhD studentship, NIHR HPRU in Environmental Exposures and Health (2021-2025)**: For developing methods to improve evidence synthesis and understand how gestational ambient air pollution exposure and the risk of preterm birth. The studentship is affiliated with the Science & Solutions for a Changing Planet DTP Cohort 8, and Transition to Zero Pollution PhD Cohort 3.
